A person’s interpretation of “The Lion King” is a great litmus test for if they’re a complete degenerate or not. 

The reality is, Timon and Pumbaa were well-meaning idiots. They were cowardly hedonists. They had the rightful king eating ze bugs like a good little Bill Gates enthusiast. They provided the archetypal “temptation in the wilderness.” 

Remain a child. Abdicate your responsibility. It’s all about your momentary pleasure. Do whatever you want. 

The king in exile’s heavenly father (and the woman he loves) reminds him who he is, and he thoroughly rejects the worldview of these “two men.” He finds his courage, and in so doing, Timon and Pumbaa also reject “Hakuna Matata.” They finally find something worth dying for. 

Hakuna Matata is the temptation. The rejection of it is virtue. 

TLDR: He turned out “fine” despite them, not because of them.

Here’s what I think the current default trajectory looks like, in "good" worlds without an AI pause:

1. The labs (or the “leading lab”, by stipulation of a responsible actor) will race as hard as they can (likely via RSI) to right before the point of superintelligence.

2. They unilaterally pause and “burn the lead”

3. They use that time to do alignment research with their existing AIs until they’re ~kinda sure that alignment is solved, or the lagging actors (via a US competitor, or a foreign one) are too close

4. The aligned (or “aligned”) AIs builds the AIs to build the AIs to build the AIs to…build aligned (or “aligned”) superintelligence.

5. The aligned superintelligence is used to obtain “decisive strategic advantage” by disabling other competing AI efforts. 

6. The lab then hands the superintelligence and the world to a democratically elected government. (6a: In some other worlds, the gov't understandably seizes the lab before this point, which might be even scarier)

7. The democratically elected government uses the superintelligence to solve non-alignment issues and then everybody lives happily ever after.

Imo this is an utterly insane plan. It has a shadow of a chance of working, but it's so ridiculously scary. It has like many different independent ways of failing and insanely reckless and undemocratic even if they do succeed at alignment, which is also dubious.

candidates.text:
Shopping turned out to be one of the biggest uses of Meta's Muse, and it doesn't buy from one shop.

If you're building in finance, I think that tells you which businesses do well once agents start managing people's money.

The first big personal finance agent will probably work like Muse: you keep one core account, and the agent shops around for everything else.

On @lennysan's  podcast, Muse's head of product says she used to buy five pairs of sweatpants from Nike. Now Muse buys them from five different shops.

Most people bank like that Nike order. Salary, savings, card and mortgage often sit with one bank, which makes much of its money from you never checking elsewhere.

An agent checks. Savings go to the safest place paying a good rate, the mortgage to the cheapest lender and FX to whoever has the tightest spread. Every financial need gets its own provider.

On a trading desk we called this best execution. Agents bring it to everyone's finances.

It fits crypto extremely well. DeFi is shared financial infrastructure that already looks like an internet full of shops, with thousands of markets open to anyone. Nobody wants to compare lending pools every night, but an agent will, and can do it 24/7.

For builders, there are probably a few good places to be:

1. The deepest market for anything that trades like a commodity
2. The best (safe) savings rate
3. The core account your agent works from
4. The rail that everything settles on
5. Services and infra for agents

And much more around agents that we can't predict now

candidates.text:
random thoughts on tech, ai, growth in general

- traditional fintech growth models always look at PayPal and Revolut but I wonder if those are the map not the territory from a different kind of market landscape
-@bbalfour work around plgs apply to markets without local confounding factors 
- @andrewchens work on local loops is more applicable to fintech because even though we have global finance, money is local and personal 
- so instead of looking at pure k factor growth bottom up like Revolut à la 2017, we should look at uber 
- @travisk breadth first search vs depth search transfers very well to fintech markets 
- instead of competing against incumbents globally, you should compete aggressively in local markets because for them to match your subsidies they have to spend proportionally more
paid acq
- looking at social media and ad growth in general it’s clear that consumers are ad blind and scroll desensitized 
- cpms are going down but cpas are going up across the board 
- this is kind of like credit spreads widening but for paid acquisition
- the natural next thought here is that perhaps instead of hyper optimizing the gto play here is … brand?  stories?  human led zigs while the media market zags toward ai slop factories and competing for the same people still clicking ads 
- organic social is also eroding, edge comes from private networks and referrals 
- ai is siloing the internet as the fyp divides society into the have-thoughts and the have-thots

ok cool so what does this mean?
- to quote @nejatian all great digital products do one of 3 things: 
1 remove friction to a problem
2 find supply or demand 
3 market make that supply and demand 
- his example was that Amazon beat eBay because it was a better marketmaker , it reduced friction 
- simplistic but you can find these in almost anything 
- Instagram beat Snapchat because it marketmade supply of ephemeral moments in the same dominant market of curated images, so it became a more efficient market than Snapchat almost instantly - so the moat is never tech, it’s always users and concept 
- with ai being able to do anything it still does nothing 
- put a chat window in front of 9/10 people and they will use it like a shitty search engine
- in general most people struggle to hold multiple abstractions in their head at the same time because of t1 and t2 thinking
- this is why we need specific drawers in kitchens, or why we struggle to buy clothes from supermarkets even though in economic utility they are ideal both in time and cost 
- the end state of all of this is a k shaped attention economy 
- permanent underclass on the fyp
- people with capital and thought reorganising around curation, private networks and human led stories 
- both arms of this economy will be huge but it leaves a vacant middle
- trying to slop together 70% quality outputs just like every other gifted and talented early years unfulfilled potential cubicle jockey is almost as bad as 30% quality because of the supply issue
- so gto is either dominate the fyp with algorot or perform exceptional cost signalling with human first storytelling , no middle ground 
- the demand side of this equation. Is hard to predict because I genuinely don’t know who will be spending in 5 years because @WillManidis commanding heights article made @citrini saaspocalypse piece look like the optimistic case 
- the actual bull case for humanity is looking at the ai capex bubble like a credit mispricing issue , 2008 wasn’t about the houses it was a self referential credit circle with moody in cahoots until abx aggregated repo pricing
- unless we get sov bailout im on the @michaeljburry bear side of the ai circlejerk, frontier labs will militech sov glaze , not take over all jobs while society muddles along with capable but not apocalyptic open models 
- regardless this odd credit environment means deep tech, hardware, bio, health, energy (nat gas esp) is undervalued

tldr long human, long rot, short middle of anything
